title: Inpatient Parkinson disease: NPO, tube, antiemetics, psychosis
scopeNote: Rounds lookup for hospitalized adults with PD on dopaminergic therapy — not a protocol. Get movement-disorder input early when the usual regimen can't be given.

rows.target: Keep the usual drugs, doses and dose times; resume the usual dose as soon as oral medication is allowed
notes: Labels: carbidopa-levodopa can continue up to anesthesia while oral medication is permitted; if interrupted, watch for an NMS-like syndrome
Abrupt reduction or withdrawal can cause hyperpyrexia, rigidity and altered consciousness — see acute-neuro:nms-parkinsonism-hyperpyrexia
Engage neurology / movement disorders early if the usual regimen can't be given (BMJ; Hwang)
evidenceNote: BMJ 2010 practice pointer: ungraded; evidence mostly case reports (authors' methods)
Sinemet and Sinemet CR PI, Interruption of Therapy: ungraded

rows.target: Reduce by no more than 2 mg/24 h, preferably every other day — don't stop abruptly
notes: Label §5.14: hyperpyrexia and confusion reported with rapid dose reduction, withdrawal or changes in antiparkinsonian therapy
sources: Neupro (rotigotine transdermal system) US prescribing information. UCB; revised 9/2026

rows.target: Give carbidopa-levodopa via NG; immediate-release tablets can be crushed
notes: Hwang: NG route for patients who can't continue their home regimen; a crushed IR dose in an acidic liquid (e.g., orange juice) is used as OFF-period rescue
Orally disintegrating carbidopa-levodopa still needs gut absorption (Hwang); BMJ cites two cases of worsening during ileus
The Sinemet IR label doesn't address crushing or tube administration — confirm flush/dispersal with pharmacy
evidenceNote: BMJ 2010 practice pointer: ungraded; evidence mostly case reports (authors' methods)
Sinemet PI: silent on tube administration
sources: Hwang H, Norris SA. Managing advanced Parkinson disease. J Geriatr Psychiatry Neurol 2021;34(4):289-300. doi:10.1177/08919887211018277

rows.target: Never crush or chew — swallow whole or half tablet
notes: If switching CR → IR for tube use: CR levodopa bioavailability is ~70–75% of IR (label Table 2); BMJ suggests ~30% lower dose when switching CR to dispersible levodopa
Label IR → CR direction: give ~10% (up to 30%) more levodopa as CR
Other ER carbidopa-levodopa products aren't covered by the provided sources
evidenceNote: Sinemet CR PI: Dosage and Administration, Table 2; Precautions (information for patients)
BMJ 2010 practice pointer: ungraded; evidence mostly case reports (authors' methods)

rows.target: Give doses on schedule; high-protein intake can delay and reduce levodopa absorption
notes: Iron salts chelate levodopa — coadminister with caution (labels)
Avoid drugs that slow gastric emptying (Hwang)
No provided source gives a feed-hold interval — follow local pharmacy/nutrition practice
evidenceNote: Sinemet and Sinemet CR PI: Precautions, Drug Interactions: ungraded

sections.heading: No reliable enteral route → rotigotine (BMJ 2010 algorithm)

rows.target: Both: oral route expected to be delayed AND ileus or another cause of poor absorption
notes: Hwang: transdermal rotigotine or SC apomorphine may be considered
evidenceNote: BMJ 2010 practice pointer: ungraded; evidence mostly case reports (authors' methods) (figure: indications box)
sources: Brennan KA, Genever RW. Managing Parkinson's disease during surgery. BMJ 2010;341:c5718. doi:10.1136/bmj.c5718
Hwang H, Norris SA. Managing advanced Parkinson disease. J Geriatr Psychiatry Neurol 2021;34(4):289-300. doi:10.1177/08919887211018277

rows.condition: Use BMJ's own factors, not calc:ledd
rows.target: A = levodopa mg/day (×0.7 if CR), then ×1.3 if on a COMT inhibitor. B = agonist mg/day × factor (ropinirole 20, rotigotine 20, pramipexole base 100, cabergoline 100, bromocriptine 10, apomorphine 10). LEDD = A + B
notes: Levodopa dose excludes carbidopa
calc:ledd uses Jost 2023 factors, which differ (CR 0.75; COMT +0.33 or +0.5 of covered levodopa; pramipexole base 142.86; rotigotine 30.3) — don't feed its result into these steps
evidenceNote: BMJ 2010 practice pointer: ungraded; evidence mostly case reports (authors' methods) (figure: LEF table)
Jost 2023 cited only for the factor comparison
sources: Brennan KA, Genever RW. Managing Parkinson's disease during surgery. BMJ 2010;341:c5718. doi:10.1136/bmj.c5718
Jost ST, et al. Levodopa dose equivalency in Parkinson's disease: updated systematic review and proposals. Mov Disord 2023;38(7):1236-1252

rows.target: Adjusted LEDD = LEDD × 0.55; rotigotine mg/24 h = adjusted LEDD ÷ 20, rounded to the nearest 2 mg, once daily
notes: BMJ rounds up to 16 mg; the US label maximum is 6 mg/24 h (early PD) and 8 mg/24 h (advanced PD) — doses above 8 mg exceed the label
Example: levodopa IR 300 mg/day → 300 × 0.55 = 165 → 8.25 → 8 mg/24 h
Example: levodopa IR 600 mg/day → 330 → 16.5 → 16 mg/24 h per BMJ (twice the label maximum)
BMJ: the ×0.55 deliberately starts below equivalence; review and adjust early; may be too weak for high-dose regimens
evidenceNote: BMJ 2010 practice pointer: ungraded; evidence mostly case reports (authors' methods) (figure: rotigotine box; text: switching section)
sources: Brennan KA, Genever RW. Managing Parkinson's disease during surgery. BMJ 2010;341:c5718. doi:10.1136/bmj.c5718
Neupro (rotigotine transdermal system) US prescribing information. UCB; revised 9/2026

rows.target: Strengths 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 mg/24 h (combine patches for the dose); don't cut; remove before MRI or cardioversion (aluminum backing — burns)
notes: Drug detectable ~3 h after application (range 1–8 h); Tmax 15–18 h; steady state in 2–3 days
No relevant PK change in renal impairment, including hemodialysis
Keep external heat off the patch — may increase absorption
Rotate sites; don't reuse a site within 14 days
Contains sodium metabisulfite (sulfite sensitivity)
sources: Neupro (rotigotine transdermal system) US prescribing information. UCB; revised 9/2026

rows.target: Acceptable — doesn't appear to worsen motor symptoms
notes: Contraindicated with apomorphine — see next row
evidenceNote: BMJ 2010 practice pointer: ungraded; evidence mostly case reports (authors' methods)
sources: Brennan KA, Genever RW. Managing Parkinson's disease during surgery. BMJ 2010;341:c5718. doi:10.1136/bmj.c5718

rows.target: Contraindicated: apomorphine with any 5-HT3 antagonist (ondansetron, granisetron, dolasetron, palonosetron, alosetron) — profound hypotension and loss of consciousness
sources: Apokyn (apomorphine hydrochloride injection) US prescribing information. MDD US Operations; revised 6/2022

rows.target: Avoid metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, promethazine, chlorpromazine, haloperidol, droperidol
notes: Apokyn §5.2 names haloperidol, chlorpromazine, promethazine, prochlorperazine and metoclopramide as worsening PD
Droperidol: class-level statement (dopamine-blocking antiemetics, Hwang); agent not named in provided sources
Metoclopramide may adversely affect disease control despite faster gastric emptying (Sinemet labels)
Dopamine antagonists may reduce the effect of rotigotine and apomorphine (labels)
evidenceNote: Apokyn PI §5.2, §7.4; Neupro PI §7.1; Sinemet PI Drug Interactions: ungraded
BMJ 2010 practice pointer: ungraded; evidence mostly case reports (authors' methods)

rows.target: Look for a trigger (infection, incl. UTI); then withdraw PD drugs in this order: anticholinergics → dopamine agonists → amantadine → MAO-B inhibitors → COMT inhibitors → levodopa
notes: Weaning carbidopa-levodopa may be limited by motor severity — then add an antipsychotic (Hwang)
sources: Hwang H, Norris SA. Managing advanced Parkinson disease. J Geriatr Psychiatry Neurol 2021;34(4):289-300. doi:10.1177/08919887211018277

rows.target: 34 mg PO once daily, no titration (10 mg with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor) — not a rapid agent: benefit shown over 6 weeks
notes: QT prolongation — avoid with other QT-prolonging drugs; avoid strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers
Capsule may be opened onto soft food; tube use not addressed in the label
Boxed warning: increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (approved only when PD-related)
evidenceNote: MDS 2019 (Seppi) Table 6: efficacious; acceptable risk without specialized monitoring; clinically useful
sources: Nuplazid (pimavanserin) capsules and tablets US prescribing information. Acadia; revised 4/2026
Seppi K, et al. Update on treatments for nonmotor symptoms of Parkinson's disease—an evidence-based medicine review (MDS). Mov Disord 2019;34(2):180-198. doi:10.1002/mds.27602

rows.target: Low dose, off-label — MDS calls it a pragmatic first choice
notes: No dose in the provided sources
No high-quality placebo RCT; similar efficacy to clozapine in clozapine-controlled trials
Blocks D2 but dissociates faster; used off-label with caution (Hwang)
evidenceNote: MDS 2019 (Seppi) Table 6: insufficient evidence; acceptable risk without specialized monitoring; possibly useful
sources: Seppi K, et al. Update on treatments for nonmotor symptoms of Parkinson's disease—an evidence-based medicine review (MDS). Mov Disord 2019;34(2):180-198. doi:10.1002/mds.27602

rows.target: Efficacious but off-label, with label ANC monitoring: baseline ANC ≥1500/µL (≥1000 in benign ethnic neutropenia), weekly for 6 months; start 12.5 mg once or twice daily
notes: Label indications are schizophrenia only
Boxed warnings: severe neutropenia; orthostatic hypotension, bradycardia, syncope (highest during titration); seizures; myocarditis/cardiomyopathy; dementia-related mortality
Anticholinergic GI hypomotility (ileus) — screen for constipation
Missed doses: 1 day → restart at 40–50%; 2 days → ~25%; longer → 12.5 mg
MDS: use when quetiapine or pimavanserin fail; can be first-line despite weekly blood counts
evidenceNote: MDS 2019 (Seppi) Table 6: efficacious; acceptable risk with specialized monitoring; clinically useful
sources: Clozapine tablets US prescribing information. Accord Healthcare; revised 10/2025

rows.target: Avoid — not efficacious, unacceptable risk
notes: Based on a low-quality negative study (MDS)
evidenceNote: MDS 2019 (Seppi) Table 6: not efficacious; unacceptable risk; not useful
sources: Seppi K, et al. Update on treatments for nonmotor symptoms of Parkinson's disease—an evidence-based medicine review (MDS). Mov Disord 2019;34(2):180-198. doi:10.1002/mds.27602

rows.target: Avoid haloperidol and other typical antipsychotics — D2 blockade can irreversibly worsen motor symptoms
notes: Also blunt rotigotine and apomorphine (labels)
sources: Hwang H, Norris SA. Managing advanced Parkinson disease. J Geriatr Psychiatry Neurol 2021;34(4):289-300. doi:10.1177/08919887211018277
Apokyn (apomorphine hydrochloride injection) US prescribing information. MDD US Operations; revised 6/2022
Neupro (rotigotine transdermal system) US prescribing information. UCB; revised 9/2026

rows.target: Use sparingly; avoid long-term — linked in time to delirium, falls and balance impairment in advanced PD
notes: Exception: benzodiazepines remain part of NMS / parkinsonism-hyperpyrexia treatment (see that entry)
sources: Hwang H, Norris SA. Managing advanced Parkinson disease. J Geriatr Psychiatry Neurol 2021;34(4):289-300. doi:10.1177/08919887211018277

rows.target: Stop anticholinergics (strongest link to psychosis and delirium); avoid opioids where possible (delirium, falls, orthostasis, constipation); wean amantadine if confusion or psychosis
sources: Hwang H, Norris SA. Managing advanced Parkinson disease. J Geriatr Psychiatry Neurol 2021;34(4):289-300. doi:10.1177/08919887211018277

pitfalls: calc:ledd (Jost 2023) and the BMJ algorithm use different factors — don't mix them
BMJ's adjusted LEDD >350 mg branch (continuous SC apomorphine with domperidone pre-load) is not on this card: the Apokyn label covers intermittent pen doses only (≤6 mg per dose)
Hallucinations, orthostasis and sudden sleep onset are dopaminergic adverse effects — consider them before adding drugs
Deep brain stimulator in situ: manufacturers advise avoiding electrocautery; bipolar diathermy if needed (BMJ)
keyNumbers: Rotigotine (BMJ 2010): LEDD (BMJ factors) × 0.55 ÷ 20 → nearest 2 mg, once daily
Neupro US max: 6 mg/24 h early PD, 8 mg/24 h advanced PD
Sinemet CR: never crush; CR levodopa ≈70–75% as bioavailable as IR
Pimavanserin 34 mg daily (10 mg with strong CYP3A4 inhibitor) — benefit over weeks
